title: Critical two-sided graph seminorm is removed by a frequency-growth obstruction
question: Does the canonical two-sided K^(-1/2)-damped q/p commutator seminorm obey a frequency-uniform onsite bound?
method: Import the exact Q3 Weyl lower bound from the critical-half authority without re-proving it in this package.
Use [q_0,W_a]=a W_a, [p_nu,W_a]=0, K>=1 and Weyl unitarity to obtain L_K(W_a)<=2a for a>0.
Set t_a=tau/a^2 and compare G tau a-B_tau against (1+C tau/a^2)2a in exact SymPy and independent Fraction lanes.
Compile Lean R211 only for rational slope arithmetic and the finite fixture inequality.
finding: Primary and independent lanes pass 19/19, integrated lane passes 21/21 and Lean R211 passes. With G=g+3 lambda=51/35 and tau=2, the lower-minus-upper difference is (32/35)a-3/2-4/a, positive at a=10 and eventually positive for all sufficiently large a. Therefore the displayed critical graph seminorm cannot satisfy the proposed frequency-uniform onsite one-step bound.
decision_reason: This is a useful route-level obstruction, not a theorem about all non-Leibniz topologies. It removes the declared K^(-1/2)-damped critical graph seminorm from the candidate tournament while leaving frequency-profiled analytic/Frechet, state-weighted, projected-Duhamel and local-strict routes open.
